title: Bioinspired Soft Robot with Incorporated Microelectrodes
protocol: Dissolve 10 g of gelatin in 100 mL of Dulbecco's phosphate-buffered saline (DPBS) using a magnetic stirrer at 50 °C.
Add 8 mL of methacrylic anhydride slowly while stirring the gelatin prepolymer solution at 70 °C for 2 h.
Dilute the reacted gelatin solution with preheated DPBS at 50 °C.
Transfer the diluted solution into dialysis membranes (molecular weight cutoff = 12–14 kDa) and place them into deionized (DI) water.
Perform dialysis at 40 °C for about 1 week.
Filter the dialyzed GelMA prepolymer solution using a sterile filter (pore size = 0.22 µm).
Transfer 25 or 30 mL of the filtered solution into 50 mL tubes and store at -80 °C for 2 days.
Freeze-dry the frozen GelMA prepolymer solution using a freeze dryer for 5 days.
Dissolve 200 mg (20% of total solution) of PEGDA (MW = 1,000) with 5 mg (0.5% of total solution) of 2-hydroxy-4-(2-hydroxyethoxy)-2-methylpropiophenone in 1 mL of DPBS.
Incubate the prepolymer solution at 80 °C for 5 min.
Dissolve 80 mg of GelMA in 4 mL of DPBS.
Add 20 mg of COOH functionalized multiwalled carbon nanotubes into the GelMA prepolymer solution.
Sonicate the MWCNT-laden GelMA prepolymer solution for 1 hour at 0.66 Hz and 100 Watt while immersed in a water bath at approximately 15 °C to prevent solvent evaporation.
Dissolve 50 mg of GelMA and 5 mg of PI in 0.8 mL of DPBS at 80 °C for 10 minutes.
Add 0.2 mL of the prepared CNT stock solution to the mixture.
Vortex the solution.
Incubate the solution at 80 °C for 10 minutes.
Wash glass slides with pure ethanol.
Stack cleaned glass slides vertically in a beaker and spread 3 mL of TMSPMA on top using a syringe.
Cover the beaker with aluminum foil to prevent evaporation of TMSPMA.
Incubate the slides in an 80 °C oven for one day.
Wash coated glass slides by dipping them into pure ethanol, then dry.
Store coated glass slides wrapped in aluminum foil at room temperature.
Fabricate a shadow mask.
Wash the glass slide with acetone.
Dry the glass slide with a compressed air gun.
Attach the shadow mask to the glass substrates using double-sided tape.
Place the assembly in an E-beam evaporator and wait until the chamber pressure reaches at least 10-6 Torr.
Deposit a 200 nm thick Au layer by E-beam evaporation (vacuum = 10-6 Torr, power = 2.6%, rate = 2 Å/s).
Cut the fabricated microelectrodes using a dicing saw machine.
Design and fabricate two photomasks to create micropatterned PEGDA hydrogel layer.
Design and fabricate another photomask to create the CNT-GelMA hydrogel layer.
Integrate Au microelectrodes between the micropatterned PEGDA and CNT-GelMA hydrogel layers.
Place 50 μm spacers made by stacking one layer of commercial invisible tape on a TMSPMA coated glass.
Pour 15 μL of 20% PEGDA prepolymer solution on top of the TMSPMA coated glass.
Cover with gold microelectrode.
Place the 1st photomask for the glass slide on top of the gold microelectrode.
Expose the whole construct to UV light at 800 mW intensity and 8 cm distance for 110 s.
Add DPBS to surround the glass slide.
Detach the micropatterned PEGDA hydrogel together with the Au microelectrodes from the uncoated glass substrate carefully after 5–10 min.
Place 100 μm spacers made by stacking two layers of commercial transparent tape on the bottom of a Petri dish.
Deposit a drop of 20 μL CNT-GelMA prepolymer solution between the spacers.
Flip the glass slide obtained and fix it onto the dish with adhesive tape.
Rotate the device upside down.
Place the 2nd photomask on top of the glass slide.
Expose under UV light at 800 mW intensity and 8 cm distance for 200 s.
Wash the obtained scaffold with DPBS and cell culture medium that includes 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS).
Leave the washed scaffold overnight in the 37 °C incubator before seeding the cells.
Isolate hearts from 2-day-old Sprague-Dawley rats following approved protocols.
Place heart pieces on a shaker overnight in 0.05% trypsin without EDTA in HBSS at a cold room temperature.
Collect heart pieces with a pipette gun and minimize the amount of trypsin.
Transfer collected heart pieces to a 50 mL tube containing 10 mL of warm cardiac media (10% FBS, 1% P/S, 1% L-glutamine).
Swirl gently in a 37 °C water bath for 7 min at approximately 60 rpm.
Remove the medium carefully from the tube with a 10 mL pipette and leave heart pieces intact.
Add 7 mL of 0.1% collagenase type 2 in HBSS to the tube.
Swirl quickly in a 37 °C water bath for 10 min at approximately 60 rpm.
Mix gently 10 times with a 10 mL pipette to disrupt heart pieces.
Remove medium carefully from the tube using a 1 mL pipette and discard.
Add 10 mL of 0.1% collagenase type 2 in HBSS to the tube.
Swirl quickly for another 10 min at approximately 120–180 rpm in a 37 °C water bath.
Check if heart pieces are dissolving completely.
Mix thoroughly with both 10 mL and 1 mL pipettes until solution appears homogeneous.
Place a 70 μm cell strainer on a new 50 mL tube.
Pipette the solution, one milliliter at a time, through the strainer.
Centrifuge the heart cell solution at 180 x g for 5 min at 37 °C.
Carefully remove all liquid above the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cells in 2 mL of cardiac media.
Add 2 mL of cardiac media from the tube wall carefully to resuspend the cells.
Transfer the suspended cells into a T175 flask with warm cardiac media drop by drop.
Place the flask in a 37 °C incubator for 1 h.
Collect the medium containing cardiomyocytes and transfer it to a 50 mL tube.
Count the cells.
Centrifuge at 260 x g for 5 min at 37 °C.
Resuspend the cells and seed them on top of the fabricated soft robot.
Pour specific volume of cardiac media with cardiomyocytes (1.95 × 10^6 cell/mL) drop by drop onto the device surface.
Incubate samples at 37 °C.
Change medium with 5 mL cell culture media containing 2% FBS and 1% L-glutamine on the first and second days after seeding.
Change medium every time the color of the medium shifts.
Remove the medium and wash cells with DPBS for 5 min at room temperature.
Fix the cells using 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) for 20 min at RT.
Wash the cells with DPBS for 5 min at RT.
Incubate the cells with 0.1% triton in DPBS at RT for 1 h.
Wash the cells 3 times with PBS for 5 min at RT.
Incubate the cells with 10% goat serum in DPBS at RT for 1 h.
Incubate the cells with a primary antibody (sarcomeric α-actinin and connexin-43) in 10% goat serum in DPBS at 4 °C for ~14–16 h.
Wash the cells 3 times with DPBS for 5 min at RT.
Incubate the cells with the secondary antibody in 10% goat serum in DPBS at RT for 1 h.
Wash the cells 3 times with DPBS for 5 min at RT.
Counterstain cells with 4',6-diamidino-2-phenylindole (DAPI) in DI water (1:1,000) for 10 min at RT.
Wash the cells 3 times with DPBS for 5 min at RT.
Take fluorescence images using an inverted laser scanning confocal microscope.
Incubate bioinspired actuators at 37 °C for 5 days.
Refresh the media on day 1 and 2 and when necessary (i.e., when the media turns yellow).
Use an inverted optical microscope to take images daily (5x and/or 10x).
Record cell movements using video capture software on the microscope's live window for 30 s at 20 frames per second (5x and/or 10x) when contractile activity starts (generally around day 3).
At day 5, detach the membranes by gently lifting from the edge with a cover slide.
Affix two carbon rod electrodes with platinum wire in a Petri dish filled with cardiac media using a 3 cm spaced PDMS holder.
Carefully transfer the soft robot into the Petri dish.
Apply a square waveform with 50 ms pulse width, DC offset value of 0 V, and peak voltage amplitude between 0.5 to 6 V on the electrodes.
Vary the frequency between 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 Hz with duty cycle between 2.5%, 5%, and 10% respectively.
Record macroscale contractions using a commercially available camera.
Attach two copper wires to the Au electrodes through an external square port using silver paste after fabrication of Au microelectrode-integrated multilayered hydrogel scaffold.
Cover the silver paste with a thin layer of PDMS precured at 80 °C for 5 min.
Put the samples on a hot plate at 45 °C for 5 h to fully crosslink the PDMS after covering the silver paste.

Apply a square wave electrical stimulus on the copper wires with DC offset value of 1 V, peak voltage amplitude between 1.5 and 5 V, and frequencies of 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 Hz respectively after seeding cardiomyocytes.
